claims.text: Controlled heat treatment can enhance hierarchical phase separation in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Increasing hierarchical phase separation through controlled heat treatment will increase the coercive field.
The relevant structural mediator is a hierarchical multiphase structure.
Hierarchical multiphase structures lead to magnetic vortex states within individual precipitates.
Magnetization reversal occurs through successive reversal of magnetic vortices.
Formation and successive reversal of precipitate-scale magnetic vortices increase coercivity.
The heat-treated alloy will have a higher coercive field than a matched untreated baseline.
The predicted effect should hold at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure.
Heat-treatment temperature, time, and atmosphere must remain within limits that avoid material degradation.
The appropriate baseline is an as-cast or annealed magnetic high-entropy alloy without the proposed controlled heat treatment.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing coercive field and microstructure between matched heat-treated and untreated samples.
Failure of the heat-treated sample to show a significantly higher coercive field than the untreated sample would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline may be described as annealed yet also as lacking controlled heat treatment, even though annealing is ordinarily a form of controlled heat treatment. The baseline and intervention are therefore not cleanly distinguished.
